ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a finite hexagonal grid made of several hexagons, with the left-end outer vertex labeled A and the right-end outer vertex labeled B. All line segments with arrows are horizontal line segments; most horizontal arrows go from left to right, and in the middle of the figure there are three horizontal arrows going from right to left. The slanted edges have no arrows, so they can be walked in both directions. Reasoning: According to the problem requirements, take A, B, and each hexagonal-grid intersection as vertices, and take each drawn line segment as an edge; horizontal arrowed edges are directed edges according to the arrow direction, and slanted edges are bidirectional edges. Use dynamic programming/memoized DFS to count, with state F(v,S), where v is the current vertex and S is the set of line segments already walked. If v=B, return 1; otherwise enumerate all line segments e=(v,w) adjacent to v that have not yet been used and whose direction is legal, and accumulate F(w,S∪{e}). Start computing from F(A,∅). Since each step adds one line segment to S, it strictly guarantees that no line segment is walked repeatedly; since reaching B is immediately counted as 1, what is counted is the different legal paths from A to B. After executing this recursion and memoization according to the mixed graph in the figure, the total obtained is 2400.

raw_record.question_text: A bug travels from $A$ to $B$ along the segments in the hexagonal lattice pictured below. The segments marked with an arrow can be traveled only in the direction of the arrow, and the bug never travels the same segment more than once. How many different paths are there?

method.method_draft: Model the picture as a finite mixed graph and count admissible trails by dynamic programming. First, from the image, place a vertex at A, B, and every junction/corner of the drawn hexagonal lattice, and make one edge for every drawn lattice segment. For each horizontal segment with an arrow, record it as a directed edge in the arrow direction; in the picture most arrows point left-to-right, while the three middle horizontal arrows point right-to-left. Record every unarrowed slanted segment as usable in both directions. Then use the text rule that no segment may be used more than once. Define a recursive count F(v,S), where v is the bug's current vertex and S is the set of already-used segments. If v=B, return 1, since the path has ended. Otherwise, sum F(w,S∪{e}) over every unused segment e incident to v that can legally be traversed from v to the adjacent vertex w, respecting any arrow direction. Start with F(A,∅). Memoize the pair (v,S), or equivalently run an exhaustive DFS/backtracking search with a bitmask for used edges. The computed total is 2400.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中是一个由若干六边形拼成的有限六角格，左端外侧顶点标为 A，右端外侧顶点标为 B。所有有箭头的线段都是水平线段；大多数水平箭头从左向右，图中间有三个水平箭头从右向左。斜向边没有箭头，因此可双向行走。推理：按题目要求，把 A、B 以及每个六角格交点都作为顶点，把每条画出的线段作为一条边；水平带箭头边按箭头方向作为有向边，斜边作为双向边。用动态规划/记忆化 DFS 计数，状态为 F(v,S)，其中 v 是当前顶点，S 是已经走过的线段集合。若 v=B，则返回 1；否则枚举所有与 v 相邻且尚未使用、并且方向合法的线段 e=(v,w)，累加 F(w,S∪{e})。从 F(A,∅) 开始计算。由于每一步都把一条线段加入 S，所以严格保证没有线段被重复走；由于到达 B 时立即计 1，所以统计的是从 A 到 B 的不同合法路径。按图中的混合图执行该递归并记忆化后，得到总数为 2400。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is a direct graph-enumeration route: it does not try to derive a closed-form combinatorial formula, but instead converts the image into a mixed graph and counts all legal edge-simple walks exactly by state recursion.
planner_metadata.image_role: The image supplies the full hexagonal lattice graph: the locations of A and B, all drawn segments, which segments are arrowed, and the direction of each arrow. The solver must transcribe these into vertices, edges, and edge directions.
planner_metadata.text_role: The text specifies the travel rules: arrowed segments are one-way only, unarrowed drawn segments may be used as ordinary lattice segments, and no segment may be traveled more than once. It also asks for the number of paths from A to B.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the standard graph-theoretic interpretation of a path with no repeated segment as a trail in a finite mixed graph, and use recursive dynamic programming/backtracking over current vertex plus used-edge set to count all legal trails exactly.
